en.title: Evidence-backed decompilation of the DOS game Larax & Zaco with REA and Ghidra
en.summary: The target is the DOS shareware game LEZAC.EXE. Using REA 6.3.0 with Ghidra, 215 functions were exported, producing per-function files, pseudocode, and assembly. Seven routines were also rebuilt in the original Pascal style, along with sixteen packet record layouts and six C routines, and all were tested extensively against the original. The result explicitly claims neither a playable game nor a bit-exact reconstruction.
en.metric: 174,777 native comparisons of Pascal against the original, plus 173,725 C-versus-original x86 cases passed

en.title: Static analysis of the Infinix X6831 arm64 kernel with REA and Ghidra on GitHub Actions
en.summary: The target is a 25,784,320-byte arm64 Image. Ghidra auto-analysis runs out of memory on a 2GB machine, so a five-stage GitHub Actions pipeline was used instead. The author wrapped the Image unmodified in a minimal ELF so REA would accept it, and wrote a custom paging driver and merge script. All three artifacts match the earlier manual analysis byte for byte by sha256.
en.metric: Image, kernel.config, and kernel.elf all match the earlier manual analysis exactly by sha256
